identification.summary: Storm-2755 is the Microsoft designation for an emerging, financially motivated threat actor that compromised Canadian employees' Microsoft 365 accounts and diverted salary payments to attacker-controlled accounts ("payroll pirate" fraud) [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft's blog (published 2026-04-09) does not state when activity was first observed; the 2026-04 value is the publication date and is an upper bound only [S1]. Microsoft says the campaign is similar in tactics to Storm-2657 (US university payroll attacks, reported October 2025) but is 'distinct in both its delivery and targeting'; the two clusters are kept separate here [S1][S3]. Secondary summaries mention an alias 'Storm-2657' for Storm-2755; this is contradicted by Microsoft's own distinction and is not adopted.

attribution.sponsor: Financially motivated; no state sponsor identified by Microsoft [S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft describes the actor as 'emerging' and 'financially motivated'; the blog states no attribution confidence level and no nationality or location of the operators [S1].
attribution.basis: Microsoft Defender Experts / Incident Response observed incident activity across several customer environments, including the actor's use of malicious infrastructure (bluegraintours[.]com) and an Axios user-agent for token replay [S1].

objectives: Financial gain by redirecting employee salary (direct deposit) payments to attacker-controlled bank accounts; Microsoft reports a direct financial loss for at least one user [S1].

targeting.notes: Microsoft says the actor 'relied exclusively on geographic targeting of Canadian users' and used industry-agnostic search terms; post-compromise activity focused on payroll, HR and finance functions rather than a specific sector [S1]. Some secondary vendor summaries claim US/Europe and healthcare/education/government victims; this was not confirmed in Microsoft's post and is not adopted.

capabilities.summary: Microsoft assesses initial access was 'likely' obtained via SEO poisoning or malvertising, with an actor-controlled domain (bluegraintours[.]com) ranking highly for queries such as 'Office 365' and misspelling 'Office 265' [S1]. Victims were sent to a fake Microsoft 365 sign-in page using adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) techniques to capture session cookies and OAuth tokens, bypassing MFA that is not phishing-resistant [S1]. The actor replayed stolen tokens with an Axios 1.7.9 user-agent while the session ID stayed constant, renewed sessions around 5:00 AM victim local time, and generated non-interactive sign-ins about every 30 minutes; some identities also saw password and MFA method changes for durable access [S1]. Discovery used intranet searches for payroll, HR, finance and admin terms, and compromised accounts emailed HR or finance staff with the subject 'Question about direct deposit' [S1]. Inbox rules hid messages containing 'direct deposit' or 'bank'; where social engineering failed, the actor manually signed in to Workday as the victim to change banking details [S1]. Activity occurred outside business hours [S1]. Microsoft notes Axios is not malicious and that the attack may have exploited CVE-2025-27152 [S1].

campaigns.name: Payroll pirate attacks against Canadian employees
campaigns.summary: Microsoft Incident Response investigated compromises of Canadian employee accounts across several customer environments via AiTM phishing, token replay, inbox-rule concealment and payroll/direct-deposit changes, including manual Workday logins; one user incurred confirmed financial loss. Microsoft engaged affected organizations and took disruption actions including a tenant takedown. Microsoft published the investigation on 2026-04-09 [S1].

diamond.adversary: Unattributed, financially motivated cluster designated Storm-2755 by Microsoft; operator identity and location not stated [S1].
diamond.capability: SEO poisoning/malvertising, AiTM token theft, Axios-based token replay, inbox rules, social engineering of HR/finance, manual Workday banking changes [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor-controlled lookalike Microsoft 365 sign-in site bluegraintours[.]com (URL indicator) and axios/1.7.9 user-agent; the post credits Push Security analysis of a related ADFS-enabled phishing page on the same domain [S1].
diamond.victim: Canadian employees with Microsoft 365 accounts and access to HR/payroll processes, selected by geography rather than sector [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Financial crime; no political or state motive stated by Microsoft [S1]. Similar payroll fraud by a distinct cluster (Storm-2657) targeted US universities in 2025 [S3].
diamond.technology: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID authentication, Exchange Online inbox rules, Workday HR/payroll SaaS, non-phishing-resistant MFA [S1].

gaps: First-observed date and campaign start are not stated in the Microsoft post.
Operator identity, nationality, and any link to Storm-2657 or other payroll-fraud clusters are not established; Microsoft states the clusters are distinct.
Total victim count, dollar losses, and affected sectors are not published (one confirmed financial loss only).
Initial access is described only as 'likely' SEO poisoning/malvertising; use of CVE-2025-27152 is stated as possible, not confirmed.
Claims by secondary vendors (US/Europe victims, specific sectors, July 2026 dating, alias Storm-2657) were not corroborated by Microsoft and were excluded.
Secondary articles (BleepingComputer, Hive Pro) could not be fetched; only search snippets were seen.
Mitigation-relevant IOCs published are minimal (one domain, one user-agent); no IP infrastructure or financial account details are public.
A social media post (X) previously cited as a source was removed because its URL was not corroborated in search results.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: the relevant environment is Microsoft 365/Entra and cloud HR/payroll SaaS (e.g., Workday) used by personnel, including DoD civilians or allied (Canadian) partner staff who use commercial identity services [S1]. Step 3: the actor is a criminal financially motivated cluster using geographic (Canada) targeting, AiTM token theft and token replay, not a state threat to operational systems [S1]. Step 4 MLCOA: continued AiTM phishing via SEO poisoning/malvertising against geographically selected users, then payroll diversion [S1]. MDCOA: expansion to other geographies or to organizations holding military/government payroll, which would affect personnel welfare and trust (not supported by cited sources; hypothetical). Candidate indicators: sign-ins with Axios user-agent matching an existing session ID, Entra error 50199 before compromise, non-interactive sign-ins about every 30 minutes, inbox rules hiding 'direct deposit'/'bank' mail, 'Question about direct deposit' emails, bluegraintours[.]com, off-hours Workday bank changes [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: share the published indicators (domain, user-agent, inbox-rule patterns) with identity and HR system owners [S1]. Authorities: response is largely defensive tenant administration (token revocation, rule removal, MFA reset) that rests with the system owner; no offensive action is implied by the sources [S1]. Mission assurance: Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant MFA, Conditional Access device compliance, blocking legacy authentication, adaptive session lifetimes and continuous access evaluation, and auditing OAuth apps, which reduce risk to workforce and personnel-pay systems [S1]. Coordination: involve identity/cloud administrators, HR/finance, and vendor (Microsoft, Workday) incident channels; Microsoft engaged affected organizations and conducted a tenant takedown [S1].
